slides.title: ACID at a table boundary
body: Atomicity: the transaction commits as a whole or does not.
Consistency and isolation operate with defined table rules.
Durability depends on the storage environment.
slides.notes: The lab observes committed writes and an intentionally rejected transaction while the local storage is available. ACID does not certify every business value or protect a deleted Colab VM. Separate the behavior of a Delta table from the durability of the machine hosting its files. The backup archive addresses the temporary runtime boundary.

slides.title: Two different versions
body: source_revision orders approved business messages.
A Delta version identifies a table commit.
A commit can affect many business records.
slides.notes: Do not use a table version as the revision of a trip. Source revision 2 means the upstream correction outranks revision 1 for that key. Delta version numbers describe transactions in the target table and can vary with valid rerun histories. Record both when explaining the correction and its audit trail.

slides.title: Schema enforcement
body: The table expects named fields and data types.
An incompatible write should stop.
An approved schema change is a separate decision.
slides.notes: A schema contract makes shape assumptions visible. It does not replace range, relationship or semantic checks. The exercise first shows enforcement, then demonstrates a controlled schema evolution on a sandbox. Keeping evolution deliberate prevents an accidental field change from silently becoming part of the serving contract.

slides.title: Constraints protect writes
body: Use required-field and value constraints where appropriate.
A negative fare violates this trip contract.
Inspect the table again after rejection.
slides.notes: A robust failure test checks more than an exception. Record the attempted invalid write, then reread the table and confirm its previous content remains intact. Zero fares are permitted here, so a non-negative rule is different from a strictly positive rule. Distance and duration follow their own positive-value contracts.

slides.title: MERGE needs an unambiguous source
body: Match one candidate to each trip_id.
Check conflicts before the update.
Apply the approved newer business state.
slides.notes: A merge is not a business-rule generator. Multiple conflicting source rows for the same target key require a documented decision before the operation. The helper validates candidates and compares source revisions. It preserves the trip grain while updating the corrected values; it does not insert a new business trip for a correction.

slides.title: Revision precedence
body: Newer approved revision: apply the update.
Older revision: keep the accepted value.
Equal revision with different values: reject the conflict.
slides.notes: Identical same-revision messages are safe replays. Conflicting messages at the same revision have no unambiguous authority under this policy. Do not resolve them merely by whichever row happens to arrive first. Preserve a clear error and the source information so the conflict can be investigated.

slides.title: Quick activity: make the decision
body: Choose a response for each message: a newer approved revision; an older revision; the same revision with conflicting business values.
Think: 1 minute. Compare: 2 minutes. Discuss: 2 minutes.
slides.notes: Use the project terms rather than naming tools without a reason. State your choice and the assumption behind it. The activity is part of the explanation time and has no separate project mark.

slides.title: Activity answer
body: Apply the newer revision, leave the accepted value unchanged for the older revision, and reject the same-revision conflict for investigation.
slides.notes: Compare the reasoning as well as the final choice. If you selected another answer, identify which meaning of a row, time boundary or business rule led to it. The project will provide an observable example of this decision.

slides.title: The correction is a value
body: SYN_T0001 changes from SAR 18.00 to SAR 23.00.
The total rises once by SAR 5.00.
Replaying the correction leaves SAR 23.00 unchanged.
slides.notes: Think of the message as the approved state of the trip, not an instruction to add five every time it is received. This is why the final table remains 75 trips and 1,880.60 SAR. The experiment checks the full relevant business content as well as the selected fare and total.

slides.title: History, time travel and RESTORE
body: History describes the table operations.
Time travel reads an available older snapshot.
RESTORE creates a new commit representing earlier state.
slides.notes: Reading an earlier version does not change the current table. RESTORE changes the current state through a new transaction; it does not erase the fact that the intervening operations happened. Both require the relevant historical files. Apply recovery experiments to the isolated copy, not to the continuing corrected project table.

slides.title: Controlled schema evolution
body: Approve the additional field explicitly.
Observe the changed schema on a sandbox.
Keep the serving fare definition unchanged.
slides.notes: The exercise adds a surcharge field in an isolated scenario. A new column is not permission to change the meaning of an existing fare measure. Inspect the before/after schema and ensure the main corrected Silver table is still the next day's source. Document how a real consumer would learn about an approved contract change.

slides.title: Compaction and logical content
body: OPTIMIZE changes the physical file layout.
The logical rows should remain equivalent.
A tiny sample cannot establish production performance.
slides.notes: Inspect the compaction operation and verify business-content equality. File count and scan time answer different questions, and no speed improvement is guaranteed for a tiny dataset. Initialization and caching can dominate measured timings. Report only the observed result and the scope of the experiment.

slides.title: VACUUM and retained history
body: The lab uses DRY RUN only.
Keep the 168-hour safety threshold.
Removing required files can break older-version reads.
slides.notes: The exercise lists candidate files without deleting them. An empty candidate list is a valid result. Data-file retention and transaction-log retention are related but different settings. The 168-hour boundary is the training rule here; an organization's actual retention requirements need their own decision and dependencies.

slides.title: A useful recovery record
body: State the attempted change and the table version.
Show the expected rejection or recovered content.

It does not test concurrent writers, broker failover or a machine crash. Clear scope makes your evidence more useful than an unqualified claim that the pipeline is production-ready.
